channel.title: Call by Reference :: CC 210 Textbook
channel.description: Finally, it is important to remember that any instantiated objects used as arguments to a method are passed in a call-by-reference manner. So, any modifications to those objects made inside of a method will also be reflected in the code that called the method. Here’s a quick example: public class Reference{ public int x; } public class Main{ public static void main(String[] args){ Reference someRef = new Reference(); someRef.x = 10; modify(someRef); System.out.println(someRef.x); // 15 } public static void modify(Reference aRef){ aRef.x = 15; } } As we can see, when we call the modify() function and pass a Reference object as an argument, we can modify the attributes inside of that object and see those changes back in the main() method after modify() is called.
